channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission Clarifies Remote Voting Rules
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission (CEC) has clarified that the restriction on remote voting outside one's polling station within the same district applies only to parliamentary elections. This restriction does not apply to the presidential election, which is held in a single nationwide district. The CEC approved amendments on November 11, 2026.

item.title: New General Director Appointed to National Electric Grid of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Rustam Sakiev has been appointed the new General Director of the National Electric Grid of Kyrgyzstan (NESK). The decision was made by the company's board of directors, as reported by the Ministry of Energy. Sakiev's priorities include ensuring reliable power supply, modernizing networks, and developing the country's energy infrastructure.

item.title: Osh to Convert 3.5 Hectares of Irrigated Farmland for Multi-Story Housing Construction
item.description: The Kyrgyz Cabinet of Ministers has approved the rezoning of 3.5 hectares of irrigated land in Osh from agricultural to residential use. The state-owned land will be used to construct a multi-story residential complex with social facilities. The Osh mayor's office is tasked with updating land records and ensuring compliance with urban planning and safety regulations.

item.title: Almaty Undertakes Major Overhaul of Housing and Utilities Infrastructure
item.description: Almaty is implementing a comprehensive modernization of its housing and utilities sector, aiming for warmer homes, more reliable networks, and an improved urban environment. Key initiatives include a national project for modernizing energy and utility sectors (2025-2029), with 105.3 billion tenge allocated for infrastructure upgrades. This involves repairing heat networks, replacing pipelines, and updating water supply systems.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Updates Rules for Mandatory Housing Insurance Against Fires and Disasters
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is proposing to update the regulations for its insurance pool, which handles mandatory housing insurance against fires and natural disasters. The draft resolution outlines a new position on the insurance pool and qualification requirements for its officials. Insurance companies must join the pool to operate, meeting financial stability and technical requirements for a unified information system.

item.title: Budget Fund Theft Uncovered in Kostanay Region; Education Head Dismissed
item.description: The prosecutor's office in the Karabalyk district of Kostanay region has uncovered budget fund theft and violations of public procurement laws. An education department head was dismissed, and seven officials faced disciplinary action. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Eliminating VAT on Potato Exports to Uzbekistan
item.description: During a visit to Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan proposed eliminating VAT on potato exports. This initiative aims to expand agricultural cooperation between the two countries, following President Sadyr Japarov's directive. Both nations agreed to ensure uninterrupted potato supplies and establish a joint venture for agricultural product processing.

item.title: Kazakhstan mobile operator owner in talks to open a digital bank
item.description: The owner of a mobile operator in Kazakhstan, VEON, has begun consultations with the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market (ARFR) regarding the opening of a digital bank. VEON aims to launch the bank by the end of 2027, integrating communication, marketplace, and banking services.

item.title: 55 New Enterprises Opened in Kyrgyzstan's Tyup District, Creating 900 Jobs
item.description: In Kyrgyzstan's Tyup district, 55 new enterprises have been established over the past five years, generating 900 job opportunities. Industrial production volume has more than doubled, according to reports presented to President Sadyr Japarov during his review of the district's socio-economic development.

item.title: Astana Airport Expansion to Acquire Land from Air Astana, SCAT, and Kazцинк
item.description: Astana's city administration plans to expropriate over 1,000 hectares across 57 land plots to expand the capital's airport. The affected lands include those belonging to airlines Air Astana and SCAT, mining company Kazцинк, and the Prosecutor General's Office. Expropriation will occur between February 2027 and February 2028.

item.title: Kazakhstan-linked hackers use AI to steal over 2,000 Tajik national security documents
item.description: A group of hackers linked to Kazakhstan has reportedly used artificial intelligence to steal over 2,000 documents related to Tajikistan's national security. Cybersecurity firm CloudSek reported that the hackers utilized an AI platform called Hermes to plan attacks, write code, and manage stolen data. The group, dubbed 'Silent Lynx,' was identified by their use of Russian language, operating during Kazakhstan's work hours, and connecting through Kazakh internet servers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes a complete ban on energy drinks starting from January 1, 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy has proposed a complete ban on the circulation of energy drinks, effective January 1, 2027. The draft law includes prohibitions on import, production, storage for sale, wholesale and retail trade, and consumption of these beverages. The proposed ban is permanent, unlike previous temporary import restrictions. The public discussion period for the bill ends on November 27.

item.title: Issyk-Kul Region Development: President Saparov Reviews Five-Year Progress
item.description: President Saparov reviewed the socio-economic development of the Issyk-Kul region's Tүp, Ak-Suu districts, and Karakol city for 2021-2026. New enterprises and jobs were created, industrial production doubled, and 128 social facilities were built. Road infrastructure was significantly improved, with major investment projects ongoing.

item.title: Tashkent Modifies Vehicle Evacuation and Storage Procedures from December 24
item.description: Tashkent will implement new rules for vehicle evacuation and storage starting December 24, 2026. Drivers can avoid towing if they arrive before loading and rectify violations. If loading begins, towing will proceed. Storage fees are calculated daily, with maximum tariffs set for towing and storage.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways Assures Normal Operations Following CEO's Detention
item.description: National company Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ) has stated it is operating normally following the reported detention of its chairman, Yeldas Otynschiev. The company confirmed that passenger and freight train services are running as scheduled and all obligations are being met.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Reviews Development in Issyk-Kul Region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov visited the Issyk-Kul region and Balykchy to review socio-economic development from 2021-2026. Funding for the Issyk-Kul district increased over 12-fold, with industrial output six times higher than in 2021. New infrastructure, including schools and roads, was built, and 2,154 jobs were created.

item.title: Uzbekistan's 2025 GDP Revised Upward to Over $169 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) for 2025 has been revised upwards by 277 trillion soums, reaching over $169 billion. The revision, based on population census results and updated enterprise reporting, increased the 2025 GDP estimate by 15% in current prices. Real GDP growth is now estimated at 7.8%, slightly higher than previous figures.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov Meets with Residents of Issyk-Kul Region
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov met with residents of the Issyk-Kul region and the city of Balykchy during his working visit. Citizens raised issues concerning socio-economic development, infrastructure, and local problems, including railway construction, water supply, road building, and land disputes. The president assured that the fight against organized crime would be intensified.

item.title: Afghanistan and Uzbekistan Finalize Agreement for 100,000 Tons of Bamyan Potatoes
item.description: Afghanistan and Uzbekistan have agreed to export 100,000 tons of potatoes from Bamyan province to Uzbekistan. The first shipment of eight trucks has already departed for Termez. This initiative aims to expand market opportunities for Bamyan farmers and strengthen bilateral trade.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Signs Law Amending Legislation on Science and National Academy of Sciences
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has signed a law amending existing legislation concerning science and the National Academy of Sciences. Adopted by the Jogorku Kenesh, the law aims to improve scientific activities, enhance efficiency, expand financial autonomy for scientific organizations, and reform the scientific system.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Warns of Potential Ethnic Strife Ahead of Elections
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has warned of potential attempts by some politicians to incite ethnic conflict between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks in the south of the country. He stated these actions could aim to destabilize the situation and influence the upcoming presidential elections. Japarov urged citizens to resist provocations and report suspicious activities to law enforcement.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains Head of Samruk-Kazyna Fund and KTZ Chairman on Corruption Charges
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee has detained Nurlan Zhakupov, chairman of the Samruk-Kazyna fund, and Yerzhan Otynshiyev, head of Kazakhstan Temir Zholy (KTZ), on suspicion of corruption. The investigation is ongoing, with details undisclosed due to secrecy. A video circulating online showed suitcases filled with cash near a residential complex in Astana, but its connection to the detentions remains unconfirmed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Pension Fund Head Discusses Potential for Doubled Pensions Through Investment Risk
item.description: The head of Kazakhstan's Unified Pension Savings Fund (ЕНПФ), Zhanat Kurmanov, stated that pensions could potentially double depending on investment portfolio choices. He noted that Kazakh citizens are currently passive in selecting investment portfolios. Kurmanov cited Hong Kong's experience, where similar issues of investor inertia exist despite multiple investment options being available.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allows Officials to Take on Side Jobs and Modifies Leave Recall Rules
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President has amended rules for officials in political, special state, and political municipal positions. They can now engage in additional paid professional activities and participate in public associations. The decree also prohibits recalling these employees from leave prematurely without their consent. These changes aim to allow officials to use their expertise while ensuring their primary duties are not compromised.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence: Transforming Public Services and Healthcare in Kazakhstan
item.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming a vital tool, transforming daily life and work processes across various sectors. In Kazakhstan, AI is increasingly utilized in public services, healthcare, education, industry, agriculture, transport, and finance. Its key advantage lies in rapid data processing, pattern identification, and process automation, saving specialists time and improving decision-making quality.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Bank Prepares 'Stop-Credit' Analog for Bank Accounts
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Bank is developing a service similar to 'Stop-Credit' that will allow citizens to prohibit the opening of new bank accounts and cards. This measure aims to prevent fraud, such as accounts being opened remotely using personal data without the owner's knowledge. The launch timeline for this new service will be announced soon.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election: 11 Candidates Submit Applications
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's presidential election candidate nomination period has closed with 11 individuals submitting applications to the Central Election Commission. Candidates must now gather at least 30,000 voter signatures by December 7, 2026, to be officially registered. The Central Election Commission is expected to finalize candidate registrations by December 23, 2026, ahead of the January 27, 2027, election.

item.title: Almaty Resident Falls Victim to Deepfake Loan Fraud Using Photo
item.description: An Almaty resident, Zukhra Valieva, became a victim of deepfake fraud after her photo was used to open four virtual accounts. Scammers then obtained loans totaling 35 million tenge in her name. Valieva questioned bank security measures and filed complaints with the police and prosecutor's office.

item.title: Kazakhstan Railways comments on detention of its head, Eljas Otynshiev
item.description: Kazakhstan Railways (KTZ) has officially commented on the detention of its head, Eljas Otynshiev, stating the company is operating normally. The National Security Committee reported Otynshiev and Samruk-Kazyna head Nurlan Zhakupov were detained on November 11 for alleged corruption.

item.title: Mangystau residents discuss President's address on Kazakhstan's development
item.description: Working groups in the Mangystau region held meetings with residents and work collectives to explain the President's address, "Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Period." Discussions focused on the address's significance for political and socio-economic development, including recent constitutional and parliamentary reforms.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree to Involve Europe in Next Peace Talks Round
item.description: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to invite European countries to the next round of peace negotiations, according to former US special envoy Jared Kushner. The agreement followed three days of intensive diplomatic talks from November 10-12. The expanded format aims to discuss not only territorial issues but also broader European security post-conflict.

item.title: Putin Allows Europe to Join Ukraine Peace Talks, Urges US to Work with Allies
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has permitted European nations to participate in peace negotiations regarding Ukraine. He stated that the US should collaborate with its European partners to determine if Europe desires peace or war in Ukraine.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Tax Incentives for New Tashkent Developers
item.description: Uzbekistan has established tax benefits and preferences for investors undertaking urban development projects in New Tashkent valued at over $50 million. These measures, outlined in a presidential decree, aim to attract investment by offering reduced profit tax rates and exemptions from land and property taxes for qualifying projects.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Ranks Among World's 50 Most Influential Muslims
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has been ranked 40th in The Muslim 500's list of the world's 500 most influential Muslims. The ranking highlights his economic liberalization, foreign investment attraction, trade expansion, education and healthcare reforms, and the end of forced labor in the cotton sector. His regional diplomacy efforts were also noted.

item.title: Arctic Ice Melt Could Intensify Drought in Parts of Eurasia, Including Western Kazakhstan
item.description: The melting of winter ice in the Barents and Kara Seas may contribute to intensified summer droughts in Eastern Europe and western Kazakhstan, according to a study in Frontiers in Water. Researchers analyzed climate data from 1940, finding a link between Arctic ice volume and reduced summer rainfall.

item.title: UFC Representatives Visit Almaty, Potential Boxing and MMA Events Discussed
item.description: Representatives from the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) have visited Almaty, Kazakhstan. Discussions are underway regarding the possibility of hosting a Zuffa Boxing event and potentially a UFC tournament in Kazakhstan next year. Previous plans for a UFC event in Astana in 2020 were canceled due to the pandemic.

item.title: SCO to Establish Anti-Terrorism and Cyber Threat Center in Tashkent
item.description: A Universal Center of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) will be established in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, to combat terrorism, extremism, and cyber threats. The center will be based at the existing SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure. A division focused on transnational organized crime will operate in Bishkek.

item.title: China's APEC Year: Key Priorities Ahead of Shenzhen Summit
item.description: Shenzhen is preparing to host leaders of Asia-Pacific economies for the APEC summit, a key event concluding China's chairmanship. China's priorities include openness, innovation, and cooperation, aiming to boost trade, implement new technologies, and reduce business barriers. Trade with APEC economies reached $3.6 trillion in Jan-Sep.

item.title: Kazakhstan Week: AI Security Summit, Tajik President Visit, CSTO Meeting, US Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan hosted the Aqaba Process summit on AI security and received Tajik President Emomali Rahmon. President Tokayev attended a CSTO security meeting in Moscow, urging joint efforts against terrorism and drug trafficking. Climate issues were discussed at COP31, with agreements worth $1.2 billion signed. Economic cooperation with the US also advanced.

item.title: New Ski Resort and Water Park Planned for Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Plans are underway to construct a ski resort in Cholpon-Ata, with an investment of 2.6 billion soms. Additionally, a water park is planned for the Kes-Senir area. These projects were presented to President Sadyr Japarov during his visit to the Issyk-Kul region.
